headline: Automated lung nodule detection has evolved from rule-based CAD to deep learning AI
dek: A Breathe publication highlighted by ERS describes the shift in automated nodule detection and its growing role in lung cancer screening.
body:
Automated lung nodule detection has evolved from rule-based computer-aided detection (CAD) systems to deep learning artificial intelligence (AI), according to a publication in Breathe highlighted by ERS publications on X.

The post said this development builds on foundational CT imaging studies from the 1990s. It added that automated detection is now playing an increasing role in lung cancer screening.

The post was published on 13 November 2026 and linked to the full article in Breathe. It did not give further details on the methods, data or conclusions of the work, so these are not reported here.
key_quote: Automated lung nodule detection has evolved from rule-based CAD systems to deep learning AI
